title: Your hero is crucial. Bring the whole army.
author: PantheonEmpiresRTS
selftext:
Sun knights, butterfly samurai, crab pirates. I wanted picking a race to start an argument before anyone trained a soldier. Then your hero runs out front, pulls a creep camp, and gives the whole army something to do.



I built Pantheon Empires on Spawn by talking with Savi. I used AI to help make it, but the decisions were mine: what belonged, what needed another pass, and what was ready to publish. My first message was:



I want to develop a fantasy age of empires combined with warcraft 3, but with large armies that still matter to the hero-centeric combat.



The army part was the point. I wanted to build and gather and train, then actually lead those troops. A powerful hero with an army reduced to scenery would have missed it.



The first faction lineup got a question from me:



Can we make the factions more unique then just humans and orcs?



Then I got specific:



Can we add another faction full of samurai butterfly people and east asian beetle bugtaurs called the Yoricho Shogunate?



That was the direction. The Saltscale Fleets needed their own way to play too. Their buildings spread sand, and they train faster on it. The crab pirates bring the beach with them. Picking another empire needed to change more than the flag.



I wanted friends beside me for the chaos, so I asked for cooperative runs in the Gauntlet. Then I changed the other cooperative mode:



Actually make the War of the Vale to Survival of the Vale and have six base spots.



Six bases, endless Ashborn waves. Different empires trying to hold the same line.



Once I started playtesting with other people, the problems stopped being hypothetical. The computer rivals needed to fight harder. Players were getting lost. u/endlessdeath chased the lag until troop orders felt as immediate as moving the hero.



One player found a particularly cruel loop in training. Train five soldiers, finish the step, lose one, and the lesson went backwards. The next step only counted if the hero landed the killing blow.



My answer eventually became:



Okay let give the tutorial a win condition. Kill the boss and you win the game easy right?



I rebuilt the training so completed steps stayed completed, army kills counted, and there was an actual finish. I also chose six empires for 1.0 and rebuilt each in the painted look. The work had shifted from adding another thing to making what was there readable.



The part I keep coming back to is how that player tried to get through the broken training. They sent their whole army into a camp and ran their hero around to pull the mobs.



That was the game I had described in my first message. They had found it. I needed to stop the tutorial fighting them.
